intro.text: Primoris Services Corporation (“Primoris”, the “Company”, “we”, “us”, or “our”) is a leading provider of critical infrastructure services operating mainly in the United States and Canada. We provide a wide range of construction, maintenance, replacement, and engineering services to a diversified base of customers through our two segments: Utilities and Energy. The structure of our reportable segments is generally focused on broad end-user markets for our services. We have longstanding customer relationships with solar facility developers, power producers, gas and electric utilities, refining, petrochemical, communications, midstream, downstream, and engineering companies, as well as transportation agencies across our core markets. We provide our services to a diversified base of customers, under a range of contracting options.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

s.t: For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, revenue derived from projects performed under MSAs was 32.0%, 36.8%, and 36.7% of total revenue, respectively.
For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, 53.1%, 41.3% and 41.1%, respectively, of total revenue was generated from our top ten customers in each year.
Our customer base is reasonably concentrated, with our top ten customers accounting for approximately 53.1% of our revenue in 2025, 41.3% of our revenue in 2024 and 41.1% of our revenue in 2023.
During 2025, 2024 and 2023, revenue attributable to our services outside of the United States, principally in Canada, was 2.3%, 4.6% and 5.8% of our total revenue, respectively.

Typically, the top ten customers in any one calendar year account for approximately 40.0 % to 50.0 % of total revenue; however, the group that comprises the top ten customers varies from year to year.
For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, approximately 53.1 %, 41.3 % and 41.1 %, respectively, of total revenue was generated from our top ten customers in each year.
For the year ended December 31, 2025, one customer accounted for approximately 12.1 % of our revenue.
For the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, no one customer accounted for more than 10% of total revenue.
Although significant materials are often supplied by the customer, we use suppliers to provide some materials and equipment used for projects.
Our ability to obtain surety bonds depends upon various factors including our capitalization, working capital, tangible net worth and amount of our indebtedness.
We depend on the continued and ongoing services of our executive officers and other key employees, including the senior management of our subsidiaries.
We rely on computer, information and communication technology and related systems to operate our business and to protect confidential, sensitive company, customer and partner information.

We rely on information technology systems, some of which are managed by third parties, to process, transmit and store electronic information and to manage or support a variety of our business processes, activities and services.

Further, customers supplying us their data rely on the security of our infrastructure and systems, including hardware, software and other elements provided by third parties, to ensure the reliability of our products and the protection of their data.
Our ability to obtain such additional financing in the future will depend on a number of factors including prevailing capital market conditions, conditions in our industry, and our operating results.

We rely on computer, information, network, and communication technology and related systems to operate our business and to protect confidential, restricted, and sensitive company, customer, and partner information.

In performing these assessments, management relies on various factors, including operating results, business plans, economic projections, anticipated future cash flows, comparable transactions and other market data.
Our primary sources of liquidity are our cash balances at the beginning of each period and our cash flows from operating activities.
The timing of share purchases, if any, depends on market conditions, share price and other factors.
